output.brief: The rejections trace to a data error in our own systems, not to the fungicide, Lower Serra growers or Meridane. When Meridane bookings moved to the new Tallis system, the mandarin product record was copied from the avocado record on 1 Aug. It carried 7.0°C instead of our 4.0°C specification. All five Meridane containers were sent with a 7.0°C instruction, and the units held 7.0°C as told. All five were rejected. Every container at 4.0°C passed, including Coastway ones packed with the new fungicide. The one Meridane container at 4.0°C passed too, and the first rejection (K3) used the old fungicide. Lower Serra fruit looked worse within rejected containers, but it was 28–40% of every load and the temperature explains the pattern. Pallet-level data in accepted containers is missing, so I'm less sure about that. Do not suspend Lower Serra, switch fungicide back, or claim against Meridane, since its controller records support its reply. Next steps, urgently: correct the Tallis mandarin record to 4.0°C. Have Meridane reset the container at sea (sailed 3 Oct) and the one queued for 10 Oct. Add a check comparing reefer settings with product specifications before submission. Review how the product master sign-off missed this. Tell Nordhafen about the cause and the fix.
